Rashi on Makkot 14a:10:1.hebrew: מאחותו דסיפא - דכתיב ערות אחותו גלה (ויקרא כ׳:י״ז):
Rashi on Makkot 14a:10:1.english: From "his sister" in the latter clause - As it is written: "The nakedness of his sister he has revealed" (Leviticus 20:17).

Rashi on Makkot 14a:11:1.hebrew: שאין עונשין מן הדין - שהרי ענש על בת אמו שלא בת אביו, ובת אביו שלא בת אמו, שנא' (שם) בת אביו או בת אמו, ויש לומר כ"ש שענש על בת אביו ובת אמו. אבל אם אמרת כך, ענשת מן הדין. לכך נאמר אחותו דסיפא:
Rashi on Makkot 14a:11:1.english: That one does not administer punishment based on an a fortiori inference - For [the Torah] imposed punishment for [relations with] his mother's daughter who is not his father's daughter, and his father's daughter who is not his mother's daughter, as it is stated (there): "The daughter of his father or the daughter of his mother." And one could say: all the more so [is he liable] for [relations with] the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother. But if you were to say this, you would have punished based on an a fortiori inference. Therefore "his sister" in the latter clause was stated:

Rashi on Makkot 14a:12:1.hebrew: גמר עונש מאזהרה - דלענין אזהרה כתיב "אחותך היא", יתירא, להזהיר על אחותו בת אביו ובת אמו, שנאמר (שם יח) "ערות בת אשת אביך מולדת אביך אחותך היא". ומה אזהרה לא חלק בין אחותו בת אביו שלא בת אמו ובין [ובת אמו שלא בת אביו] ולאחותו שהיא בת אביו ובת אמו, אף בעונש ענש על אחותו בת אביו ואמו כאחותו דבת אביו שלא בת אמו ובת אמו שלא בת אביו:
Rashi on Makkot 14a:12:1.english: He derived the punishment from the prohibition - For with regard to the prohibition it is written “she is your sister” (an extra phrase), to warn against [relations with] one's sister who is [both] his paternal and maternal sister, as it is stated (there, Leviticus 18): “The nakedness of your father’s wife’s daughter, born of your father, she is your sister.” And just as the prohibition did not distinguish between his sister from his father but not his mother [and his sister from his mother but not his father], and his sister who is [both] from his father and his mother, so too with regard to the punishment, one is punished for [relations with] his sister from both his father and mother just as for his sister from his father but not his mother, or from his mother but not his father:

Rashi on Makkot 14a:1:1.hebrew: כדאמרינן מעיקרא - טעמיה דר' עקיבא משום שתי רשעיות הוא. ודקאמרת: חייבי כריתות נמי שתי רשעיות הן — דאכתי עונש כרת עליו לא פסיקא מילתא לכרת, הואיל והוא תלוי בתשובה:
Rashi on Makkot 14a:1:1.english: As we stated initially - The reason of Rabbi Akiva is because of "two wickednesses." And when you say that those liable to karet are also [a case of] two wickednesses — [this is not so,] for still the punishment of karet is not definitively upon him; the matter is not clear-cut with regard to karet, since it is dependent on repentance:

Rashi on Makkot 14a:3:1.english: And the Rabbis - Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Makkot 14a:3:2.hebrew: לחלק - לפי שכלל כל העריות בכרת אחת, הייתי אומר: אם עשאן כולם בהעלם אחד, אינו חייב אלא אחת. לכך יצאה כרת באחותו לחלק, דהוי דבר שהיה בכלל ויצא מן הכלל ללמד על עצמו, שמתחייב עליה לעצמה אם עשאם עם חברותיה. ואם תאמר: ולא ללמד על עצמו יצא, אלא ללמד על הכלל כולו יצא: מה אחותו מיוחדת שהיא ערוה וחייבין עליה בפני עצמה, אף כל שהיא ערוה חייבין עליה בפני עצמה:
Rashi on Makkot 14a:3:2.english: To divide - Because [the Torah] included all the forbidden relations in a single karet [statement], I would have said that if one committed all of them in one lapse of awareness, he is liable only once. Therefore the karet was stated regarding his sister, to divide: for it is a matter that was included in the general category and was singled out from the general category to teach about itself — that one is liable for her separately if he committed [the transgression] with her along with her fellow [forbidden relatives]. And if you say: it was not singled out to teach about itself, but rather it was singled out to teach about the entire category: just as his sister is distinct in that she is a forbidden relation and one is liable for her on her own, so too every [woman] who is a forbidden relation, one is liable for her on her own.

Rashi on Makkot 14a:4:1.hebrew: מואל אשה - דמצי למכתב "ולנדה לא תקרב":
Rashi on Makkot 14a:4:1.english: From "And to a woman" - For [the Torah] could have written, "and to a menstruating woman you shall not approach."

Rashi on Makkot 14a:5:1.hebrew: לחייבו על אחותו ועל אחות אביו כו' - אם בא על שלשתן בהעלם אחד:
Rashi on Makkot 14a:5:1.english: To render him liable for his sister and for his father's sister, etc. - If he engaged in intercourse with all three of them in a single lapse of awareness.

Rashi on Makkot 14a:6:1.hebrew: הרי שמות מוחלקין - שיש אזהרה בכל אחת, והרי הן כשאר כל העריות:
Rashi on Makkot 14a:6:1.english: Behold, the names are divided - For there is a warning in each one, and behold, they are like all the other forbidden relations.

Rashi on Makkot 14a:6:2.hebrew: ברשיעא בר רשיעא - הבא על אמו והוליד שתי בנות, וחזר ובא על אחת מהן והוליד בן, ובא הבן על אחות אמו, שהיא אחותו ואחות אביו:
Rashi on Makkot 14a:6:2.english: In the case of a wicked person, son of a wicked person - One who engaged in intercourse with his mother and fathered two daughters, and then went back and engaged in intercourse with one of them and fathered a son; and the son then engaged in intercourse with his mother's sister, who is [also] his own sister and his father's sister.

Rashi on Makkot 14a:7:1.english: In the meat market - In a place where they sell meat in the butcher shops.

Tosafot on Makkot 14a:5:1.hebrew: לאפוקי הני - פסח ומילה דבקום עשה נינהו, קשה ל"ל היקשא לאפוקי פסח ומילה? תיפוק ליה מדאמרינן בת"כ: ועשה אחת יצא מסית ומדיח ומקלל אביו ואמו ועדים זוממין, שאין בהן מעשה, דאין בהן קרבן; וה"ה פסח ומילה, דאי מימנע ולא עביד ליכא מעשה. ושמא י"ל דאצטריך דרשא דהכא, משום דבת"כ איכא דרשא אחריתי, דמפרש מסית ומדיח דלאו בני קרבן נינהו, משום דבעינן דומיא דעבודת כוכבים דיש בו כרת, ופסח ומילה הוו בכרת, והוה אמילא דהויין בקרבן. מיהו ממילה קשה, למה לי קרא? דהא לא הויא בכרת דומיא דעבודת כוכבים, דהא לעולם לא יתברר שיהא בכרת עד שימות, דלעולם יכול למול עצמו וליפטר מכרת. וי"ל דלעולם כל זמן שלא מל עונש כרת עליו:
Tosafot on Makkot 14a:5:1.english: To exclude these - [The laws of] the Paschal offering and circumcision are positive commandments, [so] it is difficult: why do I need the analogy (hekesh) to exclude the Paschal offering and circumcision? Let him derive it from what we say in the Torat Kohanim: "'And one' – this excludes the inciter, the enticer, one who curses his father and mother, and conspiring witnesses," which involve no act, [and] for which there is no offering; and the same applies to the Paschal offering and circumcision, for if one refrains and does not perform [them], there is no act. And perhaps one can say that the derivation here is needed because in the Torat Kohanim there is another derivation, which explains that the inciter and the enticer are not subject to an offering because we require [a case] similar to idolatry, which carries karet; and the Paschal offering and circumcision are subject to karet, and it would have been presumed that they are subject to an offering. However, regarding circumcision it is difficult: why do I need a verse? For it is not subject to karet in a manner similar to idolatry, since it is never established that he is subject to karet until he dies, for he can always circumcise himself and be exempted from karet. And one can say that always, as long as he has not circumcised, the punishment of karet is upon him:

Tosafot on Makkot 14a:5:2.hebrew: ההוא מיבעי ליה לחייבו על אחותו שהיא בת אביו ובת אמו - וא"ת: ל"ל כרת בקדושים? תיפוק ליה גבי אזהרה, כתיב "אחותך היא", יתירא, לאחותו בת אביו ובת אמו. וכתיב (ויקרא י״ח:כ״ט): "ונכרתו הנפשות העושות"! וי"ל: דונכרתו לא קאי אלא אעריות המפורשות בהדיא. ונהי דבקרא כתיב "ערות בת אשת אביך מולדת אביך אחותך היא", מ"מ מיירי טפי מאחותו שהיא מאשת אביו ובת אביו. אבל בת אביו ובת אמו (ומאונסים) לא ידעינן אלא מיתורא דקרא, "אחותך היא":
Tosafot on Makkot 14a:5:2.english: That [verse] is needed to render him liable for his sister who is the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother - And if you ask: Why do I need [the verse about] karet in Kedoshim? Let him derive it from the warning, where it is written "she is your sister," which is superfluous, [to include] his sister who is the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother. And it is written (Leviticus 18:29): "And the souls that do them shall be cut off"! And one can answer: The phrase "shall be cut off" refers only to the forbidden relations that are explicitly stated. And although it is written in the verse, "The nakedness of your father's wife's daughter, born of your father, she is your sister," in any case it speaks more of his sister who is from his father's wife and his father's daughter. But [a sister who is] the daughter of his father and the daughter of his mother (and from forcibly conceived [relations]) we know only from the superfluous wording of the verse, "she is your sister":

Tosafot on Makkot 14a:9:1.hebrew: ואידך - רבי יצחק גמר עונש מאזהרה. תימה: דבכריתות פ"ק (דף נ.) א"ר יצחק עונשין מן הדין, דקאמר לר' יצחק כדאית ליה ולרבנן כדאית להו, לומר דאין עונשין מן הדין. וכן לקמן בפרקין (מכות דף יז:) דקאמר "אפי' למאן דאמר עונשין מן הדין" כו', ופי' דהיינו ר' יצחק. ותימה, דבכל שינויי דהכא משמע דשפיר אית ליה לר' יצחק דאין עונשין מן הדין. ונראה דלהאי שינויא דקאמר גמר עונש מאזהרה, סבר ר' יצחק עונשין מן הדין, דהכי פירושא: גמר עונש מאזהרה משום דאיכא קל וחומר להענישן, וכיון דהשוום באזהרה הוא הדין נמי בעונש, כיון דאיכא קל וחומר להענישן. ומעתה אמר רבי יצחק בכל דוכתי נמי עונשין מן הדין, דהיינו היכא שאין צריך לענין אזהרה. ומהאי טעמא היכא דגמיר עונש מאזהרה היינו דוקא דאיכא להענישו מן הדין, דאם לא כן בחייבי לאוין נמי, כגון גבי ממזר עמוני, נילף בהם עונש כרת מהאי טעמא דגמר עונש מאזהרה, דכי היכי דהשוום לענין אזהרה הוא הדין לענין עונש. אלא כדפי' דדוקא משום דאיכא להענישו מן הדין קאמר גמר (גמר) עונש מאזהרה. כך נראה למשי"ח, וצריך עיון:
Tosafot on Makkot 14a:9:1.english: And the other - Rabbi Yitzchak derives the punishment from the warning. It is puzzling: for in Keritut, chapter one (50a), Rabbi Yitzchak said, "We do impose punishments by logical inference," where [the Gemara] says that [this applies] to Rabbi Yitzchak according to his own view, and to the Rabbis according to theirs, [the Rabbis] holding that we do not impose punishments by logical inference. And so too later in our chapter (Makkot 17b), where it says, "Even according to the one who says that we impose punishments by logical inference," etc., and [Rashi] explained that this is Rabbi Yitzchak. And it is puzzling, for in all the answers here it implies that Rabbi Yitzchak does hold that we do not impose punishments by logical inference. It appears that according to this answer, which says that he derives the punishment from the warning, Rabbi Yitzchak holds that we do impose punishments by logical inference. For this is its meaning: he derives the punishment from the warning because there is an a fortiori inference to punish them; and since they were equated in the warning, the same applies to the punishment, since there is an a fortiori inference to punish them. And from now on, Rabbi Yitzchak said that in all places too we impose punishments by logical inference, namely where [the verse] is not needed for the warning. And for this reason, [the principle] that where he derives the punishment from the warning, it is specifically where there is a way to punish him by logical inference; for if not, then in the case of those liable for [violating] prohibitions as well, such as an Ammonite mamzer, let us derive for them the punishment of karet for this reason, that he derives the punishment from the warning, since just as they were equated regarding the warning, so too regarding the punishment. Rather, as I explained, it is specifically because there is a way to punish him by logical inference that he says he derives the punishment from the warning. So it appears to my teacher, and it requires further study:
